verses.1: A psalm of Asaph. God rises in the divine council, gives judgment in the midst of the gods.
verses.2: "How long will you judge unjustly and favor the cause of the wicked? Selah
verses.3: Defend the lowly and fatherless; render justice to the afflicted and needy.
verses.4: Rescue the lowly and poor; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
verses.5: The gods neither know nor understand, wandering about in darkness, and all the world's foundations shake.
verses.6: I declare: "Gods though you be, offspring of the Most High all of you,
verses.7: Yet like any mortal you shall die; like any prince you shall fall."
verses.8: Arise, O God, judge the earth, for yours are all the nations.

notes.text: The gods are blind and unable to declare what is right. Their misrule shakes earth's foundations (cf Psalm 11:3; 75:4), which God made firm in creation (Psalm 96:10).
I declare: "Gods though you be": in John 10:34 Jesus uses the verse to prove that those to whom the word of God is addressed can fittingly be called "gods."

Judge the earth: according to Deut 32:8-9, Israel's God had originally assigned jurisdiction over the foreign nations to the subordinate deities, keeping Israel as a personal possession. Now God will directly take over the rulership of the whole world.
